definition_en: a fixed period of time, a word with a special meaning, a condition of an agreement, or a school period
core_image: 一块立在时间线上的界石，也立在词典与合同里
scene: 新学期第一课，老师在黑板上写下这门课最难的术语。 Students must learn the technical terms of biology.
sceneCN: 这里 term 是「术语」（第 2 个义项：专门领域的固定用语）；句意：学生必须学习生物学的专业术语。

collocations.phrase: under the terms of the contract

senses.title: A fixed period of time
senses.definition: a set length of time, especially a school term or an office term
senses.definitionCN: 固定的时段，尤指学期或任期
senses.example: The autumn term begins in September.
senses.exampleCN: 秋季学期九月开始。
senses.why: The root is a boundary stone: a term is the space between two marks in time.
senses.whyCN: 词根是界石：term 就是时间线上两个界标之间的一段。

senses.title: A word with a special meaning
senses.definition: a word or expression with a precise meaning in a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域具有精确含义的词或表达
senses.example: Photosynthesis is a basic term in botany.
senses.exampleCN: 光合作用是植物学的基本术语。
senses.why: A boundary in language: the word marks exactly where one meaning stops and another begins.
senses.whyCN: 语言中的界石：这个词精确标出意义与意义之间的边界。

senses.title: A condition of an agreement
senses.definition: one of the conditions of a contract or agreement, usually plural
senses.definitionCN: 合同或协议的条件之一，多用复数
senses.example: They agreed to the terms of the lease.
senses.exampleCN: 他们同意了租约条款。
senses.why: Terms are the boundary lines drawn inside an agreement: each clause ends a dispute before it starts.
senses.whyCN: 条款是协议内部的界线：每一条都在争执发生前划下终点。

senses.title: A way of expressing something
senses.definition: the particular words or style used to express something, in terms of or in plain terms
senses.definitionCN: 表达某事所用的话语或风格，用于 in terms of 等
senses.example: Explain the plan in simple terms.
senses.exampleCN: 用简单的措辞解释这个计划。
senses.why: Choosing terms is placing markers in speech: the same thing can be fenced with different words.
senses.whyCN: 选词就是在言语里立界标：同一件事可以用不同的词围出不同的说法。

senses.title: To give a name to
senses.definition: to describe or name something in a particular way, usually passive
senses.definitionCN: 以特定方式称呼或描述，多用被动
senses.example: The project was termed a great success.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目被称为巨大成功。
senses.why: To term is to attach a fixed label, fixing the boundary of what a thing shall be called.
senses.whyCN: to term 就是贴上固定标签，划定某物名称的边界。

senses.title: The end of a pregnancy or of life
senses.definition: the end of a pregnancy carried full time, or the end of life, in full term or in terminally ill contexts
senses.definitionCN: 妊娠足月，或生命的末期，见于 full term 等
senses.example: The baby was born at full term.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿足月出生。
senses.why: The boundary sense returns literally: the end mark of gestation or of life.
senses.whyCN: 「界石」义字面回归：妊娠或生命终点的标记。

intro.en: Term comes from Latin terminus, the boundary stone, the same root as terminal and terminate.
intro.cn: term 源自拉丁语 terminus「界石」，与 terminal、terminate 同根。

items.en: Terminus named a boundary stone and its guardian god.
items.cn: terminus 既指界石，也是守护边界之神的名字。

items.en: The deeper origin of terminus is debated; links to words for stake or fixed mark are proposed but unproven.
items.cn: terminus 的更早来源有争议；与「木桩、固定标记」的联系有此一说但未确证。

items.en: Old French terme passed the word to English in two shapes of meaning: time-limit and expression.
items.cn: 古法语 terme 把「时限」与「用语」两义传给英语。

items.en: Medieval schools fixed the school-term sense and logic used term for a concept word.
items.cn: 中世纪学校确立了学期义，逻辑学用 term 指概念词。

items.en: Contracts, science and computing multiplied the word: terms of service, term paper.
items.cn: 契约、科学与计算使该词激增：服务条款、学期论文。

note.en: Term is compared with its boundary-word family and with words for periods and expressions.
note.cn: 把 term 与「界石」词族及表示时段、用语的词对比。

entries.definition: at the end; an end station
the past form of the verb term
entries.definitionCN: 动词 term 的过去式

entries.definition: a word or phrase used to say something
the last time by which something must be done

normalIntro.en: Real links: terminus the stone, the school calendar, contract clauses, and in terms of.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：界石 terminus、校历、合同条款、in terms of。

normal.en: Terminus marks where the field stops; term marks where time or meaning stops.
normal.cn: terminus 标记田地止步处；term 标记时间或意义的止步处。

normal.en: The autumn term is a fenced stretch of the year.
normal.cn: 秋季学期是被围起来的一段年历。

normal.en: Technical terms are words with fences around them.
normal.cn: 术语就是围了栅栏的词。

normal.en: Come to terms with it: draw the boundary and accept it.
normal.cn: come to terms with：划下界线并接受。

normal.en: In the long term: beyond the next boundary stone.
normal.cn: in the long term：越过下一块界石之后。

abstract.en: A term is a fence you agree to stand inside.
abstract.cn: term 是你同意站进去的一道栅栏。

abstract.en: Every definition begins by placing a stone.
abstract.cn: 每个定义都从立一块石头开始。

abstract.en: To name a thing is to end its vagueness.
abstract.cn: 为事物命名，就是终结它的模糊。

examples.en: The new term starts on the first Monday of September.
examples.cn: 新学期于九月第一个周一开学。

examples.en: Photosynthesis is a term every biology student learns.
examples.cn: 光合作用是每个生物学生都要学的术语。

examples.en: Read the terms before you sign the contract.
examples.cn: 签约前先读一遍条款。

root: 拉丁语 terminus「界石、端点」→ 古法语 terme → 英语 term；本义为边界，引申为时间边界（学期、期限）、语言边界（术语、措辞）。

sensesIntro.en: One stone, many fences: the calendar term, the contract term, the technical term.
sensesIntro.cn: 一块石头，多种栅栏：校历的学期、合同的条款、专业的术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone planted in time and in language.
core.cn: 核心意象：插在时间与语言里的界石。

branches.en: The calendar is a row of stones.
branches.cn: 日历是一排界石。

branches.en: A term fences one meaning inside a field.
branches.cn: 术语把一个意义围在领域之内。

branches.en: Clauses are fences agreed by two hands.
branches.cn: 条款是两只手共同竖起的栅栏。

branches.en: To speak is to place stones in the air.
branches.cn: 说话就是在空中立石。

branches.en: The body also keeps its own calendar.
branches.cn: 身体也保有自己的历法。

intro.en: Term shares the terminus family with terminal, terminate and terminology.
intro.cn: term 与 terminal、terminate、terminology 同属 terminus 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin terminus, boundary stone, is the base; its deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 词基为拉丁语 terminus「界石」；其更早来源不确定。

definition_en: a large fighting force on land, or a very large group of people
core_image: 一队士兵整齐走过广场
scene: 一队士兵排成整齐的行列走过广场。 The army marched through the town.
sceneCN: 这里 army 是「军队」（第 1 个义项：一支作战部队）；句意为军队列队穿过城镇。

senses.title: A land fighting force
senses.definition: a large group of soldiers trained to fight on land
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、在陆地上作战的大批士兵
senses.example: The army marched through the town.
senses.exampleCN: 军队列队穿过城镇。
senses.why: The root meant armed, so a large body of armed people is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为武装的，所以一大群武装的人就是第一义。

senses.title: A very large group
senses.definition: a very large number of people or things moving together
senses.definitionCN: 一大群一起行动的人或物
senses.example: An army of helpers cleaned the park.
senses.exampleCN: 一大批帮手清理了公园。
senses.why: So many people acting as one resemble a marching force, which gives the group sense.
senses.whyCN: 那么多人像一支行进的队伍一样行动，于是有「大批」的义项。

intro.en: The recorded history of army is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 army 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Armata meant an armed force.
items.cn: armata 意为武装力量。

items.en: Arma meant weapons of war.
items.cn: arma 意为作战的武器。

items.en: French armee named a body of armed men.
items.cn: 法语 armée 指一群武装的人。

items.en: English borrowed army for a force fighting on land.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪借入 army，指在陆地作战的部队。

items.en: Today it also pictures a great crowd of helpers.
items.cn: 今天它也画出「一大批帮手」这样的画面。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The plural for more than one force.
A general word for an organised body of fighters.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指有组织的作战力量。

entries.definition: It names soldiers as a group.
A single person in the force.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The Latin armata meant armed: an army is a great many armed people marching as one.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 armata 意为武装的：army 就是一大群武装的人整体行进。

normal.en: The same family also gives armies and arm.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 armies 与 arm。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase join the army.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「参军」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of army in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 army 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: a large fighting force on land, or a very large group of people.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「军队」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a line of soldiers marching across a square.
abstract.cn: 想象一队士兵整齐走过广场。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: Her brother joined the army last year.
examples.cn: 她哥哥去年参军了。

examples.en: The army marched through the town.
examples.cn: 军队列队穿过城镇。

examples.en: An army of helpers cleaned the park.
examples.cn: 一大批帮手清理了公园。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of army grows from one core image: a line of soldiers marching across a square.

branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：大批。

branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：军队、大批。

definition_en: a group of people who play or work together, or to join with someone to do something
core_image: 几匹马被同一副挽具套在一起
scene: 整支球队在雨里坚持训练。 The whole team kept training in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 team 是「队、队伍」（第 1 个义项）；句意：整支球队在雨里坚持训练。

senses.title: A group that plays together
senses.definition: a group of people who play a sport on the same side
senses.definitionCN: 在同一方参加比赛的一个人群
senses.example: The whole team kept training in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 整支球队在雨里坚持训练。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a set of animals yoked to one load.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是被同一副挽具套住、共同拉东西的一组牲口。

senses.title: A group that works together
senses.definition: a group of people who work together on a task
senses.definitionCN: 为完成一项任务而共同工作的一群人
senses.example: A team of engineers designed the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一组工程师设计这座桥。
senses.why: The yoked animals became any group pulling one goal.
senses.whyCN: 被套在一起的牲口，变成任何朝同一目标用力的群体。

senses.title: To join with someone
senses.definition: to join another person or group to do something together
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人或群体联合做事
senses.example: The two firms teamed up on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司在这个项目上合作。
senses.why: To be in one team is to be yoked to the same task.
senses.whyCN: 在同一个队里，就是被套上同一件差事。

intro.en: Team first meant a set of animals pulling one load.
intro.cn: team 最初指共同拉一副载重的一组牲口。

items.en: The root meant a pulling group.
items.cn: 词根意为共同拖拉的一群。

items.en: Team meant a set of draft animals.
items.cn: team 指一组役畜。

items.en: Team extended to any group with one purpose.
items.cn: team 扩展到任何目标一致的群体。

items.en: Team named sports sides and work groups.
items.cn: team 指运动队与工作组。

items.en: The verb means joining forces.
items.cn: 动词义为合力合作。

note.en: Team is compared with look-alike forms and with words for groups.
note.cn: 把 team 与形近形式以及表示群体的词作对比。

branches.en: The sports side is the daily sense.

branches.en: Group and joining are two sides.

definition_zh: 国际的；国际性的；国际比赛
definition_en: involving two or more countries, or belonging to the whole world rather than one nation
core_image: 一张长桌，桌边插着好几面不同颜色的国旗
scene: 会议厅里长桌两侧坐着不同语言的代表，同声传译耳机排成一行。 The treaty became international law after the vote.
sceneCN: 这里 international 是「国际的」（第 1 个义项：涉及多个国家的），句意为表决之后该条约成了国际法。画面里的物件：长桌、国旗、传译耳机。

pos.zh: 形容词：国际的；国际性的
名词：国际比赛；国际组织成员

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在国际上」
由本词加 -ism 构成，义为「国际主义」
由本词加 -ize 构成，义为「使国际化」
去前缀 nation 加 -al 构成，义为「国家的」

senses.title: Between nations
senses.definition: existing or happening between two or more countries
senses.definitionCN: 存在于或发生在两个以上国家之间的
senses.example: Both sides signed an international agreement on fishing rights.
senses.exampleCN: 双方签署了一份关于捕鱼权的国际协议。
senses.why: The prefix inter- means between, so the word literally places something between nations.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 inter- 意为「之间」，所以这个词字面上就是把某物放在各国之间。

senses.title: Open to many countries
senses.definition: made up of or open to people and groups from many nations
senses.definitionCN: 由许多国家的人或团体组成、或向他们开放的
senses.example: The orchestra has an international cast of players.
senses.exampleCN: 这个乐团的演奏者来自许多国家。
senses.why: If something lies between nations, it naturally gathers people from all of them.
senses.whyCN: 既然位于各国之间，自然就会把各国的人都聚到一起。

senses.title: Competition or body
senses.definition: a match between national teams, or an organization with member states
senses.definitionCN: 国家代表队之间的比赛，或有成员国参加的组织
senses.example: He won three internationals before he turned twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 他二十岁前赢了三场国际比赛。
senses.why: As a noun the adjective needed no new shape: the games themselves became internationals.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时形容词不必变形：这类比赛就被叫作 internationals。

intro.en: International was coined in English in the late eighteenth century by adding inter- to national.
intro.cn: international 是十八世纪晚期英语在 national 前加 inter- 新造的词。

items.en: Inter meant "between" and nasci "to be born".
items.cn: inter 意为「之间」，nasci 意为「出生」。

items.en: Nation entered French from Latin natio, a people born together.
items.cn: nation 从拉丁语 natio「同出生的一群人」进入法语。

items.en: English used national for what belongs to one people.
items.cn: 英语用 national 表示属于一个民族或国家的。

items.en: Jeremy Bentham coined international for law that binds nations.
items.cn: 杰里米·边沁造出 international，指约束各国的法律。

items.en: From law the word spread to trade, sport, and organizations.
items.cn: 这个词从法律扩展到贸易、体育与各类组织。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same inter- and nat- parts; the near-meaning group holds words about worldwide scale.
note.cn: 形近组共用 inter- 与 nat- 两部分；近义组收表示全球范围的词。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「国家的；民族的」，只属于一国。

entries.definition: Happening inside one country or object.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内部的」，强调在内部。

entries.definition: A period of time between two events.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「间隔」，指两事之间的时间。

entries.definition: Covering the whole world as a single unit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「全球的」，强调整体范围。

entries.definition: Spread through every part of the world.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「遍及全世界的」。

entries.definition: Operating in several countries at once.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「跨国的」，指同时在多国运作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks break the word into pieces you already know.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它拆成你早已熟悉的几块。

normal.en: inter- means between; national means of a nation.
normal.cn: inter- 是「之间」，national 是「国家的」。

normal.en: Put them together: what sits between nations.
normal.cn: 合起来：坐在各国之间的东西。

normal.en: An international airport serves flights from other countries.
normal.cn: 国际机场接待来自别国的航班。

normal.en: Drop inter- and you are back to one country.
normal.cn: 去掉 inter- 就退回一个国家。

normal.en: The word was born in law, not in sport.
normal.cn: 这个词先在法律里出生，而不是体育。

abstract.en: International is the gap turned into a meeting room.
abstract.cn: 国际就是那道缝隙被改造成一间会议室。

abstract.en: A border is a line; international is what crosses it.
abstract.cn: 边界是一条线；国际是跨过这条线的一切。

abstract.en: Many flags, one word on the door.
abstract.cn: 许多面国旗，门牌上只写一个词。

examples.en: She works for an international charity in Geneva.
examples.cn: 她在日内瓦一家国际慈善机构工作。

examples.en: International calls cost extra on that plan.
examples.cn: 那个套餐里国际长途要另外收费。

examples.en: The match was his first international at this level.
examples.cn: 这场比赛是他在这一级别的首次国际赛事。

dict_mnemonic.text: inter（之间）+ nation（国家）+ al——国家之间的

root: 拉丁语 inter「之间」+ natio「出生、族群」→ 古法语 nation → 英语 national → 加 inter- 成 international。同族有 nation、national、internationally。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: between nations, made of many nations, and as a noun for big matches or bodies.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：国与国之间的、由多国组成的，以及作名词指国际赛事或组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room where more than one flag stands at the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌边立着不止一面国旗的房间。

branches.en: THE TREATY: agreements that bind more than one state.
branches.cn: 条约这条线：约束不止一个国家的协定。

branches.en: THE TEAM: people drawn from many countries.
branches.cn: 团队这条线：来自许多国家的人。

branches.en: THE FIXTURE: a match or a body named for its scope.
branches.cn: 赛事这条线：以范围命名的比赛或组织。

branches.en: THE FRAME: both senses hang on what lies beyond one border.
branches.cn: 框架线：两个义项都挂在同一条边界之外。

branches.en: THE STAGE: a shared stage makes both the team and the match possible.
branches.cn: 舞台线：共用的舞台让团队与比赛都成为可能。

intro.en: International is inter- "between" plus national, where nat- means born.
intro.cn: international 是 inter-「之间」加 national，其中 nat- 意为「出生」。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter and natio are recorded; the verb nasci is the oldest member.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 与 natio 均有记载，动词 nasci 是这一族最古老的成员。

items.example: It marks what sits between two sides.
items.exampleCN: 它标出位于两侧之间的东西。

items.example: The root also appears in native and nature.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 native 与 nature。

items.example: The noun grew into the modern nation.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词演变成现代的 nation。

items.example: It makes national out of nation.
items.exampleCN: 它把 nation 变成 national。

items.example: The noun names one political community.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指一个政治共同体。

items.example: The word adds inter- to this adjective.
items.exampleCN: 本词就是在这个形容词前加 inter-。

definition_zh: 亲爱的；昂贵的；亲爱的（称呼）；哦，天哪
definition_en: loved or much liked; costing a lot of money; a name for someone you love
core_image: 从心里捧出来的一个温柔称呼
scene: 生日那天，奶奶递给我一张亲手写的贺卡。 My grandmother started the card with the word Dear, which made me smile.
sceneCN: 这里 dear 是「亲爱的」（第 1 个义项：被心捧着的人）；句意是奶奶在贺卡开头写了 Dear，让我笑了。

collocations.zh: 亲爱的李小姐（书信称呼）

derivatives.zh: 由 dear 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「深切地；昂贵地」
由 dear 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「亲爱；贵重」
由 en-（使）加 dear 构成，义为「使受喜爱」
由 dear 的旧形加 -ling 构成，义为「心爱的人」

senses.title: Loved or much liked
senses.definition: loved by someone or very much liked
senses.definitionCN: 被某人爱着或非常讨人喜欢
senses.example: My dear friend helped me carry the heavy books home.
senses.exampleCN: 我亲爱的朋友帮我把沉重的书搬回家。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the heart's attachment, because a person held close in feeling receives this warm label.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的意义是心的依恋：一个人被感情紧紧捧着，便得到这个温柔的称呼。

senses.title: Costing a lot of money
senses.definition: costing a lot of money
senses.definitionCN: 价钱很高
senses.example: In that shop everything is too dear for students.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店里的东西对学生来说都太贵了。
senses.why: What you treasure is precious, and precious things cost much, so the feeling of treasuring stretched to price.
senses.whyCN: 被珍爱的东西显得贵重，贵重的东西价格高，「珍视」的心情便延伸出「昂贵」的价钱义。

senses.title: A name for someone you love
senses.definition: a word used when talking to someone you love
senses.definitionCN: 对所爱之人的称呼用语
senses.example: Come here, dear, and have some soup.
senses.exampleCN: 过来吧，亲爱的，喝点汤。
senses.why: People speak the feeling out loud, so the adjective turned into a calling word for loved ones.
senses.whyCN: 把心里的爱说出口，形容词便变成呼唤亲人的名词性称呼，这是感情直接长出的用法。

senses.title: A cry of surprise
senses.definition: an exclamation showing surprise or worry
senses.definitionCN: 表示惊讶或担忧的感叹语
senses.example: Oh dear, I left my homework at home!
senses.exampleCN: 哦，天哪，我把作业忘在家里了！
senses.why: A worried cry borrows a soft word, because small troubles call for gentle surprise.
senses.whyCN: 遇到小麻烦的惊呼借用了这个温柔的词，因为轻微的慌张适合用亲昵的语气来表达。

intro.en: Dear traces back to an Old English word for something precious.
intro.cn: dear 可追溯到古英语中表示「珍贵的」的一个词。

items.en: The word deore meant precious, valuable or beloved.
items.cn: 古英语 deore 意为珍贵的、有价值的、被爱的。

items.en: It belongs to a Germanic family of words about value and love.
items.cn: 它属于日耳曼语族中关于价值与爱的词族。

items.en: The spelling became dere and then dear, and the beloved sense stayed strong.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写经历 dere 再到 dear，「所爱」的义项一直稳固。

items.en: Writers also used it for things that cost much, since beloved things feel precious.
items.cn: 作家也用它指花钱多的东西，因为被珍爱之物显得贵重。

items.en: It settled into letters and greetings as a polite opening word, and British English keeps the old price sense.
items.cn: 它固定为书信礼貌的开头称呼；英式英语仍保留旧的价钱义。

note.en: These words belong to the affection family or share the gentle sound of dear.
note.cn: 这些词属于亲爱词族，或与 dear 有相似的温柔读音。

entries.definition: in a loving or strong way
a fast animal with horns, different root
entries.definitionCN: 鹿（与 dear 同音，词源无关）

entries.definition: to have courage to do something
entries.definitionCN: 敢；敢于（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: Use the heart image and the dear family to lock in the word.
normalIntro.cn: 用「心捧」的画面和 dear 词族来锁定这个词。

normal.en: dear to me means held close in my heart.
normal.cn: dear to me 表示在心里被捧得很近。

normal.en: Dear is the first word of many letters.
normal.cn: Dear 是许多书信的第一个词。

normal.en: deer sounds the same but has four legs.
normal.cn: deer 与 dear 同音，但它是有四条腿的鹿。

normal.en: dearly is the adverb: love someone dearly.
normal.cn: 副词是 dearly：love someone dearly（深爱某人）。

normal.en: For price, expensive is the safer word today.
normal.cn: 表示价钱如今用 expensive 更稳妥。

abstract.en: Picture a heart held in two warm hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗被双手捧着的心。

abstract.en: Hear the soft tone people use when calling a loved one.
abstract.cn: 听一听人们呼唤所爱之人时的温柔语气。

abstract.en: Feel the small shock of a tiny mistake, oh dear.
abstract.cn: 体会出了小差错时轻轻一声 oh dear 的心情。

examples.en: She wrote Dear Grandma at the top of the letter.
examples.cn: 她在信的开头写了 Dear Grandma（亲爱的奶奶）。

examples.en: This bag is too dear for me; let's find a cheaper one.
examples.cn: 这个包对我来说太贵了，我们找个便宜点的吧。

examples.en: Oh dear, the school bus is leaving without me.
examples.cn: 哦，天哪，校车要开走了，落下我了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘀儿」——像妈妈轻轻喊你「嘀儿，过来」，就是「亲爱的」的语气

root: 来自古英语 deore（珍贵的、被爱的），属日耳曼语族的价值词族；「昂贵」义由「珍贵」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: Dear moves from a heart feeling to a price tag and a greeting.
sensesIntro.cn: dear 从心底的感情，扩展到价钱标签和书信称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something precious held close
core.cn: 核心意象：被捧在手边的珍贵之物

branches.en: A person loved by the heart
branches.cn: 被心爱着的人

branches.en: A thing that costs much
branches.cn: 价钱高的东西

branches.en: A soft calling word
branches.cn: 温柔的称呼语

branches.en: From feeling to spoken greeting
branches.cn: 从感情到说出口的称呼

branches.en: Precious things and small shocks
branches.cn: 贵重之物与小惊呼

intro.en: Dear is a short word with a small family around it.
intro.cn: dear 是个短词，周围有一圈小词族。

latinIntro.en: Dear is Germanic, so it has no Latin relatives here.
latinIntro.cn: dear 属日耳曼语源，这里没有拉丁同族词。

items.exampleCN: my dearest friend（我最亲爱的朋友）
dearness of memory（记忆中的亲厚）
endear oneself to others（让人喜爱自己）
a deer in the forest（林中的鹿）
my beloved school（我心爱的学校）
hold old photos dear（珍视旧照片）

definition_en: to consider someone or something in a particular way; respect or esteem; to look at steadily
core_image: 老师把一份作业翻看两遍，然后缓缓点头
scene: 老师把那份作业翻来覆去看了两遍，最后缓缓点了点头。 The teacher regarded the essay as the best in the class.
sceneCN: 这里 regarded 是 regard 的过去式，取「看待」（第 1 个义项：以某种眼光认为）；句意为老师认为这篇作文是全班最好的。画面里可留意：翻看两遍的动作、缓缓点头。

senses.title: To consider in a way
senses.definition: to think of someone or something in a particular manner
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式认为某人或某物
senses.example: The teacher regarded the essay as the best in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师认为这篇作文是全班最好的。
senses.why: The word begins with a steady look: to regard a thing is first to fix the eyes on it, and then to fix a judgment on it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始于凝神一看：先让目光落在某物上，再让判断落在它上面。

senses.title: Respect or esteem
senses.definition: a feeling of admiration and careful attention toward someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的钦佩与郑重对待
senses.example: The old craftsman is held in high regard by everyone in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上人人都十分敬重这位老匠人。
senses.why: When the steady look carries weight, it becomes esteem: the one who is looked at long is the one who is valued.
senses.whyCN: 当这种凝神注视带上分量，它就变成敬重：被看得最久的人，也是被看重的人。

senses.title: To look at steadily
senses.definition: to look at someone or something with attention, often without speaking
senses.definitionCN: 带着注意看某人或某物，常常不出声
senses.example: She regarded the stranger for a long moment before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她注视了那陌生人好一会儿才答话。
senses.why: This is the plainest sense, and it keeps the original image of eyes held on a face.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的一义，它保留了「目光停在一个人脸上」的原始意象。

intro.en: Regard is a French word of watching: a Germanic verb of guarding took a French prefix, and English received it as a steady look.
intro.cn: regard 是一个来自法语的「看」的词：日耳曼语的「看守」动词接上法语前缀，英语接收它时意为凝神注视。

items.en: A Germanic verb of watching and guarding lies behind the French word for looking.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表「看守、注视」的动词，是法语「看」这个词的后盾。

items.en: Old French garder meant to guard or keep, and English kept it as guard.
items.cn: 古法语 garder 意为看守、保留，英语把它保留为 guard。

items.en: Regarder added the intensive prefix re- and meant to look at closely.
items.cn: regarder 加上加强语气的前缀 re-，意为仔细地看。

items.en: English took regard as both a look and a care, and the verb followed the noun.
items.cn: 英语把 regard 同时用作「注视」与「关切」，动词义随后跟上。

items.en: High regard and kind regards grew from the same root: attention paid becomes respect, and respect becomes a greeting.
items.cn: high regard 与 kind regards 出自同一词根：投去的注意变成敬重，敬重又变成问候。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the French verb of guarding; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of judging and looking.
note.cn: 形近组收由法语「看守」动词构成的词；近义组收表示评判与观看的动词。

entries.definition: To think of in a certain way.
To regard in a particular way.

normalIntro.en: The word is a long look: first the eyes rest on a thing, then the mind decides what it is worth.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一次长久的注视：先让目光停在某物上，再让心思判定它值多少。

normal.en: Regard as means to hold an opinion about something.
normal.cn: regard as 指对某物持某种看法。

normal.en: To regard a person is to look, and to regard them highly is to look up.
normal.cn: regard 一个人是看，regard 得高就是敬重。

normal.en: In this regard is a formal way of saying in this matter.
normal.cn: in this regard 是「在这方面」的正式说法。

normal.en: Give my regards means pass on my greetings.
normal.cn: give my regards 指代我问候。

normal.en: Regardless drops the regard, and carries on without looking.
normal.cn: regardless 丢掉了「看」，不瞧一眼就继续。

abstract.en: How we regard a person decides how we treat them.
abstract.cn: 我们如何看待一个人，决定了我们如何对待他。

abstract.en: To be held in high regard is to be looked at with care.
abstract.cn: 被十分敬重，就是被郑重地看待。

abstract.en: A regard that never becomes action is only a look.
abstract.cn: 从不化为行动的尊重，只是一眼注视。

examples.en: The teacher regarded the essay as the best in the class.
examples.cn: 老师认为这篇作文是全班最好的。

examples.en: The old craftsman is held in high regard by everyone in the town.
examples.cn: 镇上人人都十分敬重这位老匠人。

examples.en: She regarded the stranger for a long moment before answering.
examples.cn: 她注视了那陌生人好一会儿才答话。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（一再）加 gard（看守、看）：一再地看一个人，就是在打量他、评价他、敬重他。

root: 日耳曼语 wardon（看守）→ 古法语 garder（看守）→ regarder（仔细看）→ 英语 regard；re- 在此是加强语气的前缀，词根并非拉丁语，因此拉丁条目只列前缀以外的法语与英语形式。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a steady look; the senses move from forming a view, to holding someone in esteem, to watching silently.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「凝神的注视」；义项从形成看法，到把人放在敬重的位置，再到默默观看。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teacher reading an essay twice and then nodding slowly.
core.cn: 核心意象：老师把一份作业翻看两遍，缓缓点头。

branches.en: an essay called the best
branches.cn: 被评为最好的一篇作文

branches.en: an old craftsman respected by a town
branches.cn: 被全镇敬重的老匠人

branches.en: a stranger watched before an answer
branches.cn: 答话前被注视的陌生人

branches.en: a look that turns into a standing
branches.cn: 注视升为声望

branches.en: watching first, judging after
branches.cn: 先看，后判断

intro.en: A Germanic verb of guarding took a French prefix of intensity, and the compound passed into English as a steady, weighing look.
intro.cn: 日耳曼语表「看守」的动词接上法语中表加强的前缀，这个复合词进入英语，意为凝神而带分量的注视。

latinIntro.en: The stem is the French garder of Germanic origin; re- here intensifies rather than repeats, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是源自日耳曼语的法语 garder；这里的 re- 表加强而非重复，因此不列拉丁词根。

definition_en: a chart showing the days and months of a year, the system used to arrange them, or a list of planned dates
core_image: 墙上挂着一本按月翻页的日历
scene: 每年一月，她都会在日历上圈出家人的生日。 Every January she circles family birthdays on the calendar.
sceneCN: 这里 calendar 是「日历」（第 1 个义项：显示一年日期与月份的表格）；句意为每年一月她都在日历上圈出家人的生日。

derivatives.zh: 由 calendar 加 -ical 构成，义为「历法上的」
由 calendar 加 -ing 构成，指「按日历排期」

senses.title: The chart of the year
senses.definition: a chart that shows the days, weeks and months of a year
senses.definitionCN: 显示一年中日期、星期与月份的表格
senses.example: Every January she circles family birthdays on the calendar.
senses.exampleCN: 每年一月她都在日历上圈出家人的生日。
senses.why: The Latin kalendae named the first day of each month, and the list of those days became the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 kalendae 指每月的初一，而这些日子的清单就成了日历。

senses.title: The system of arranging days
senses.definition: a system that fixes the length and order of months and years
senses.definitionCN: 规定月份与年份长度和顺序的体系
senses.example: The lunar calendar sets the date of the Spring Festival.
senses.exampleCN: 农历决定了春节的日期。
senses.why: Once the chart of days grew into a rule for counting whole years, it was also called a calendar.
senses.whyCN: 当记日的表格发展成计算整年的规则，它也被称为一种历法。

senses.title: A list of planned dates
senses.definition: a list of events and the dates on which they will happen
senses.definitionCN: 列有活动及其日期的清单
senses.example: The school calendar lists every exam week.
senses.exampleCN: 学校的日程表列出了每个考试周。
senses.why: Modern offices turned the paper chart into a schedule, and the same word followed.
senses.whyCN: 现代办公把纸面日历变成了日程安排，同一个词也随之沿用。

intro.en: Calendar goes back to the Latin kalendae, the first day of the month, when accounts were recorded.
intro.cn: calendar 可上溯到拉丁语 kalendae，即每月的初一，那天要记录账目。

items.en: Kalendae was the first day of the Roman month, when accounts were entered.
items.cn: kalendae 是罗马每月的初一，账目在那天登记。

items.en: A calendarium was the account book that listed those first days.
items.cn: calendarium 是列出这些初一的账本。

items.en: Old French softened the word into calendier and passed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语把词形软化为 calendier，再传给英语。

items.en: Middle English calendar meant both the table of months and the book of accounts.
items.cn: 中古英语 calendar 既指月份表，也指账本。

items.en: Today a calendar can be a wall chart, a whole system, or a schedule.
items.cn: 今天 calendar 可以是墙上挂历、一整套历法，或一份日程。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second collects time-keeping words.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收计时相关的词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「压光机」，比 calendar 少一个 a。

entries.definition: A bowl with holes used for draining food.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「滤锅」，读音与 calendar 接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Latin origin, the real compounds and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的拉丁语来源、真实复合词和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Latin kalendae was the first day of the month, and the list of those days became the calendar.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 kalendae 是每月初一，这些日子的清单就成了日历。

normal.en: The old calendarium was an account book, which is why a calendar still lists dates in order.
normal.cn: 古时的 calendarium 是账本，所以日历至今按顺序列出日期。

normal.en: A calendar can be a wall chart, a lunar system, or a school schedule.
normal.cn: calendar 可以是挂历、农历体系，也可以是学校日程。

normal.en: It often pairs with lunar, academic, year and app.
normal.cn: 它常与 lunar、academic、year、app 搭配。

normal.en: Spell c-a-l-e-n-d-a-r; the second a is easy to drop.
normal.cn: 拼写是 c-a-l-e-n-d-a-r，第二个 a 很容易漏掉。

abstract.en: See a wall chart with one page for each month: that chart is a calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象一张墙上挂着的表，每个月一页：那张表就是 calendar。

abstract.en: Turn the page and the chart becomes a plan for the whole year.
abstract.cn: 翻过一页，这张表就变成整年的计划。

abstract.en: Hang the picture of the wall chart in your mind and let it name the word.
abstract.cn: 把这张挂历的画面挂在心里，让它替你记住这个词。

examples.en: Every January she circles family birthdays on the calendar.
examples.cn: 每年一月她都在日历上圈出家人的生日。

examples.en: The lunar calendar sets the date of the Spring Festival.
examples.cn: 农历决定了春节的日期。

examples.en: The school calendar lists every exam week.
examples.cn: 学校的日程表列出了每个考试周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡伦德」——墙上按月翻页的那本东西：日历

root: calendar 可上溯到拉丁语 kalendae，指罗马每月的初一，那天人们要登记账目。由此产生的 calendarium 就是账本，里面按顺序列出每个月的初一。这个词经古法语 calendier 进入英语，写成 calendar，既指月份表，也指账本。后来它分化为两层意思：纸面的日期表格是「日历」，背后的记日规则是「历法」；现代办公又把同一份表格变成排活动的「日程表」。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of calendar grow from one picture: an ordered list of days.
sensesIntro.cn: calendar 的三个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一份按顺序排好的日子清单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall chart whose pages turn month by month
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上挂着一本按月翻页的日历

branches.en: THE CHART: the printed list of days is the first sense.
branches.cn: 表格线：印好的日子清单是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: the rule behind the list is the second sense.
branches.cn: 体系线：清单背后的规则是第二个义项。

branches.en: THE PLAN: the same list used for events is the third sense.
branches.cn: 计划线：同一份清单用来排活动就是第三个义项。

branches.en: THE ORDER: chart and system both depend on counting days.
branches.cn: 顺序线：表格与体系都依赖数日子。

branches.en: THE YEAR: a system of months becomes a plan across the year.
branches.cn: 年度线：月份体系延展成整年的计划。

intro.en: Calendar is a base noun, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: calendar 是基础名词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin kalendae and calendarium are the recorded forms behind the word, so they are listed as the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 kalendae 与 calendarium 是这个词背后的有记录形式，因此作为直接来源列出。

definition_en: to think carefully about something before deciding, or to believe something is true
core_image: 捧着问题在心里反复掂量
scene: 选社团前，他把时间和兴趣都摆在心里称了称。 Consider joining the science club this term.
sceneCN: 这里 consider 是「考虑」（第 1 个义项：认真思索再决定）；句意是考虑一下这学期加入科学社。

derivatives.zh: 由 consider 加 -ation 构成，义为「考虑；体贴」
由 consider 加 -able 构成，义为「相当大的；可观的」
由 consider 加 -ing 构成，义为「考虑到；鉴于」

senses.title: To think carefully before deciding
senses.definition: to think about something carefully in order to decide
senses.definitionCN: 为了做决定而认真思考
senses.example: We considered moving the match to Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们考虑过把比赛挪到周六。
senses.why: The Latin prefix con- means together and sidus means star: you study the stars together to plan your move.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 con- 表示「一起」，sidus 表示「星辰」，古人合观星辰以定行止。

senses.title: To believe something is a fact
senses.definition: to have an opinion that something is true or of a kind
senses.definitionCN: 持有某物为真或属某类的看法
senses.example: Most students consider the library the quietest place.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数学生认为图书馆是最安静的地方。
senses.why: Weighing a thing in the mind fixes where you place it.
senses.whyCN: 在心里掂量过后，你会给它安个位置。

senses.title: To think about others' needs
senses.definition: to pay attention to other people's feelings or needs
senses.definitionCN: 注意到别人的感受与需要
senses.example: A good captain considers every player's energy.
senses.exampleCN: 好队长会顾及每位队员的体力。
senses.why: Careful thinking naturally includes the people around you.
senses.whyCN: 认真思考自然会把身边的人算进去。

senses.title: To look at with attention
senses.definition: to observe something thoughtfully
senses.definitionCN: 聚精会神地观察某物
senses.example: The old painter considered the sketch for a long time.
senses.exampleCN: 老画家对着草图端详了很久。
senses.why: The earliest sense was the eyes, before the mind took over.
senses.whyCN: 最初义在眼，后来才移到心。

intro.en: Consider may go back to watching the stars.
intro.cn: consider 的源头可能与「观星」有关。

items.en: Latin sidus meant a star or constellation.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sidus 意为星辰、星座。

items.en: Latin considerare meant to observe the stars, thought to mean studying carefully.
items.cn: 拉丁语 considerare 意为观察星辰，一般认为引申为仔细审视。

items.en: Latin considero developed into thinking over a matter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 considero 逐渐指反复思量一件事。

items.en: Old French considerer carried the thinking sense.
items.cn: 古法语 considerer 传下「思考」之义。

items.en: Middle English consideren meant both to look at and to think.
items.cn: 中古英语 consideren 兼指注视与思量。

items.en: Modern English consider settled into decide-thinking and opinion.
items.cn: 现代英语 consider 固定为「决策前思考」与「认为」。

note.en: The first group collects the sid family; the second collects words close in meaning.

normalIntro.en: Remember consider through stars and weighing.

abstract.cn: 想象水手观星择路。

abstract.en: Feel a friend saving you the window seat.
abstract.cn: 感受朋友为你留出靠窗座位。

examples.en: Consider your schedule before joining two clubs.
examples.cn: 报两个社团前先考虑一下时间安排。

examples.en: We consider honesty the most important rule in our class.
examples.cn: 我们把诚信视为班里最重要的守则。

branches.en: A captain caring for tired players

definition_zh: 使满意；满足；符合；使信服
definition_en: to make someone pleased or content; to fulfil a need or desire; to meet a requirement; to convince someone
core_image: 把对方需要的东西刚好给足
scene: 优质服务能满足顾客。 Good service can satisfy customers.
sceneCN: 这里 satisfy 是「使满意」（第 1 个义项）；句意：优质服务能满足顾客。

senses.title: To please someone
senses.definition: to make someone feel pleased or content
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到愉快或满足
senses.example: The gift satisfied the child.
senses.exampleCN: 这份礼物让这个孩子很满意。
senses.why: The base sense is giving someone enough to be happy.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是给对方足够的东西使其高兴。

senses.title: To fulfil a need
senses.definition: to provide enough to meet a need, desire, or appetite
senses.definitionCN: 提供足以满足需要、欲望或胃口的东西
senses.example: A snack will satisfy your hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 一份点心就能让你不饿。
senses.why: A need is like an empty space that must be filled.
senses.whyCN: 需要就像一个必须被填满的空缺。

senses.title: To meet a requirement
senses.definition: to meet a rule, condition, or standard
senses.definitionCN: 达到规则、条件或标准
senses.example: The team must satisfy the entry rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍必须符合参赛规则。
senses.why: The idea of enough applies to formal conditions.
senses.whyCN: 「足够」的观念适用于正式条件。

senses.title: To convince
senses.definition: to give someone enough proof to remove doubt
senses.definitionCN: 提供足以消除疑问的证据
senses.example: The evidence satisfied the jury.
senses.exampleCN: 证据使陪审团信服了。
senses.why: Proof fills the space of doubt until nothing is left to question.
senses.whyCN: 证据填满疑问的空间，直到无可质疑。

intro.en: Satisfy comes from Latin satisfacere, from satis enough and facere to make.
intro.cn: satisfy 来自拉丁语 satisfacere，由 satis（足够）与 facere（做）构成。

items.en: Satis means enough.
items.cn: satis 意为足够。

items.en: Facere means to make or do.
items.cn: facere 意为做。

items.en: Satisfacere means to make enough.
items.cn: satisfacere 意为做到足够。

items.en: Satisfier carries the sense of paying a debt.
items.cn: satisfier 带有偿还债务之义。

items.en: Satisfy means to please, fulfil, or convince.
items.cn: 现代英语中 satisfy 意为使满意、满足或使信服。

note.en: Satisfy means to give enough; satiate means to fill to excess.
note.cn: satisfy 是给足，satiate 则是过度填满。

entries.definition: to fill beyond what is wanted
to satisfy fully, often too much
to carry out a need or promise

normalIntro.en: Satisfy works for people, needs, rules, and doubts alike.
normalIntro.cn: satisfy 的对象可以是人、需要、规则或疑问。

normal.cn: 这个答案没能让老师满意。

normal.en: He ate bread to satisfy his hunger.
normal.cn: 他吃面包充饥。

normal.en: The product satisfies all safety standards.
normal.cn: 该产品符合所有安全标准。

normal.en: She satisfied the judges that she was right.
normal.cn: 她使评委相信她是对的。

normal.en: Are you satisfied with the service?
normal.cn: 你对服务满意吗？

abstract.en: Picture a cup filled exactly to the right level.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子被倒到恰到好处的高度。

abstract.en: Imagine a lock clicking shut on the last number.
abstract.cn: 想象密码锁在最后一个数字咔哒合上。

abstract.en: Think of doubt melting once proof arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象证据到来后疑问随之消融。

examples.en: It is impossible to satisfy everyone.
examples.cn: 不可能让所有人都满意。

examples.en: The meal satisfied our appetite.
examples.cn: 这顿饭满足了我们的胃口。

examples.en: Candidates must satisfy the language requirement.
examples.cn: 考生必须符合语言要求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: giving exactly enough to fill a need.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 satis 与 facere 组合成 satisfacere，即 satisfy 的源头。

items.meaning: to give enough and make content

items.exampleCN: 这个计划符合每个条件。

definition_zh: 严肃的；严重的；认真的；重大的

senses.definitionCN: 对某事真诚而认真

senses.why: A serious person means what they say.

senses.title: Important

senses.definitionCN: 重要到需要认真对待

senses.exampleCN: 我们面临一个重大决定。

items.en: Serius meant weighty or grave.

items.cn: 它也用来形容严重的问题与伤势。

note.en: Serious is compared with similar-looking words and with words for gravity.
note.cn: 把 serious 与形近词以及表示严重的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Serious means heavy in manner, in harm, or in importance.
normalIntro.cn: serious 意为神情、危害或重要性上的沉重。

normal.en: A serious face shows no joke.
normal.cn: 严肃的脸上没有玩笑。

normal.en: A serious injury needs a doctor.
normal.cn: 重伤需要医生。

normal.en: She is serious about her studies.
normal.cn: 她对待学业很认真。

normal.en: The adverb is seriously.

normal.en: The noun is seriousness.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 seriousness。

abstract.en: What matters asks for our full attention.

abstract.en: To be earnest is to mean what one says.
abstract.cn: 认真就是言出必真。

examples.en: We face a serious decision.
examples.cn: 我们面临一个重大决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: serious 出自拉丁语 serius（有分量的），本义「沉重的」，后指神情严肃、情况严重、态度认真与事关重大。

root: 源自拉丁语 serius（有分量的、严肃的），核心义「沉重而有分量」。

sensesIntro.en: Serious means not joking, very bad, sincere, or important.
sensesIntro.cn: serious 意为严肃的、严重的、认真的或重大的。

core.cn: 需要被认真对待的分量。

branches.en: A face without a joke.
branches.cn: 不带玩笑的面孔。

branches.en: Harm that is hard to undo.
branches.cn: 难以挽回的伤害。

branches.en: Sincerity in what one does.
branches.cn: 做事时的真诚。

branches.en: A choice with large consequences.
branches.cn: 后果重大的选择。

branches.en: Harm and importance both carry weight.
branches.cn: 危害与重要性都带着分量。

intro.en: Serious belongs to the Latin serius family of weight and gravity.
intro.cn: serious 属于拉丁语 serius（沉重）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin serius is the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 serius 是历史词根。

items.example: He understood the seriousness of it.
The hall was full of solemnity.
The severity of the pain shocked her.
